quote: Except when traffic is being controlled by a police officer or a traffic-control signal: When proper signs have been erected, the driver of a vehicle shall stop or yield at a clearly marked stop line or, if there is none, before entering the crosswalk on the near side of the intersection or, if there is none, then at the point nearest the intersection where the driver has a view of approaching traffic on the through highway. After having stopped or, in the event of a yield sign, slowed or stopped, the driver shall yield the right-of-way to other vehicles which have entered the intersection from such through highway or which are approaching so closely on such through highway as to constitute an immediate hazard during the time such driver is moving across or within the intersection.

activation.condition: proper sign governs a vehicle approaching the through-highway intersection, absent police-officer or traffic-signal control

obligation.description: stop or yield at the stated reference hierarchy, then yield to through-highway vehicles already entered or approaching closely enough to constitute an immediate hazard while crossing or within the intersection

exceptions.trigger: traffic controlled by police officer or traffic-control signal
exceptions.effect: subsection-1 signed-intersection duty does not govern under that control
exceptions.replacement_obligation: unresolved under the controlling officer or signal rule
exceptions.source_clause: Except when traffic is being controlled by a police officer or a traffic-control signal:

timing.description: stop/yield reference precedes entry; through-highway priority is assessed during the ego crossing or within-intersection interval

judgment_calls_needed.note: Sign face, placement and governance require original Native and pixel evidence.

judgment_calls_needed.phrase: point nearest the intersection where the driver has a view of approaching traffic on the through highway
judgment_calls_needed.note: Sampled collision rays do not establish the nearest legally sufficient human view.
The statute supplies no numerical hazard cutoff.
Body and speed histories alone do not decide legal priority.
